Fracture mechanisms: 2

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A direct lateral force bends a long bone, producing tension on one cortex and compression on the other. A triangular wedge fragment is present. Which mechanical loading pattern best explains this fracture configuration?

  1. Torsional loading
  2. Axial compression
  3. Traction avulsion
  4. Fatigue fracture
  5. Bending force
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Bending force

Bending creates tension on one side and compression on the other and may produce a wedge fragment.

Understanding the options

Bending force
Bending creates tension on one side and compression on the other and may produce a wedge fragment.
Torsional loading
Twisting forces commonly produce spiral shaft fractures. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Axial compression
Axial loading can cause impaction or collapse in susceptible bone. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Traction avulsion
A forceful tendon or ligament pull can detach a bony attachment. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Fatigue fracture
Repetitive abnormal loading can fracture otherwise normal bone. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
